original_question: Suppose a k-type immersion x : M -> E^m has spectral decomposition x = c + x1 + ... + xk, and for each i the subspace Ei is spanned by the values x_i(p) as p ranges over M. The immersion is called linearly independent when E1, ..., Ek are linearly independent. Study and classify linearly independent 2-type immersions.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 7: "Study and classify linearly independent 2-type immersions." This is the exact open problem your draft is aiming at. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact target, uses the same notion of a linearly independent immersion via the spectral subspaces E_i, and correctly specializes the open problem to the 2-type case. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
missing_details: The paper’s ambient setting is an isometric immersion x:M→E^m of a connected Riemannian manifold M into real Euclidean m-space E^m; this should be stated explicitly. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

The spectral decomposition is not just a formal sum: x=c+x_1+⋯+x_k with c constant and each x_i a nonconstant E^m-valued eigenmap of the Laplace operator Δ, satisfying Δx_i=λ_i x_i. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

For 'k-type' in the paper, the eigenvalues λ_1,…,λ_k are required to be mutually distinct; in the 2-type case one needs λ_1≠λ_2. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

To make 'linearly independent' stand-alone, one should say that E_1 and E_2 are linearly independent as subspaces of E^m, i.e. their sum is direct. Section 6 introduces the terminology but relies on the standard linear-algebra meaning. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

The question should stay narrowly on Problem 7 itself and not drift to the neighboring Problem 8 on codimension 2 or to the separate notion of orthogonal immersions, even though those are discussed in the same section. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

No additional homogeneity, polynomial degree, nilpotency, characteristic, or 'for all sufficiently large m' condition belongs to this problem; adding any of these would depart from the paper’s formulation. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
refined_question: Let x:M→E^m be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into real Euclidean m-space. Assume x is of 2-type, meaning that its position vector field admits a spectral decomposition x=c+x_1+x_2, where c∈E^m is constant, x_1 and x_2 are nonconstant E^m-valued maps, and Δx_i=λ_i x_i for distinct real eigenvalues λ_1 and λ_2, with Δ the Laplace operator of M. For i=1,2, let E_i⊂E^m be the subspace spanned by {x_i(p): p∈M}. Determine and classify those 2-type immersions for which E_1 and E_2 are linearly independent subspaces of E^m. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper, because Section 6 first defines linearly independent immersions using the spectral subspaces E_i and then states, verbatim, Problem 7: 'Study and classify linearly independent 2-type immersions.' The only substantive repairs needed are to import the preliminaries that make the statement self-contained: x is an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into real Euclidean space, the decomposition is a Laplacian spectral decomposition, and '2-type' means the two eigenvalues are distinct. The nearby discussion in Section 6 also shows that the intended scope is exactly Problem 7, not the neighboring codimension-2 classification problem or the later restricted-type discussion. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
